review.title: Failure to claim a property tax exemption
review.plain: Failing in any year to claim, in the manner required by law at the time, an exemption or classification that reduces a property tax is deemed a waiver of it for that year.

provisions.what: The failure in any year to claim, in a manner required by the laws in effect at the time the claim is required to be made, an exemption or classification which reduces a property tax shall be deemed a waiver of the exemption or classification for that year
conditions: The failure in any year to claim, in a manner required by the laws in effect at the time the claim is required to be made, an exemption or classification which reduces a property tax

review.title: Exempting low-value real property
review.plain: With two-thirds of each house concurring, the Legislature may authorize county boards of supervisors to exempt real property worth so little that its taxes and subventions would be less than the cost of assessing and collecting them.
powers: may authorize county boards of supervisors to exempt real property

provisions.what: The Legislature, two-thirds of the membership of each house concurring, may authorize county boards of supervisors to exempt real property having a full value so low that, if not exempt, the total taxes and applicable subventions on the property would amount to less than the cost of assessing and collecting them
conditions: two-thirds of the membership of each house concurring

review.title: Open space and historical property valuation
review.plain: The Legislature may define open space land and property of historical significance, and must provide that when such land or property is enforceably restricted, it is valued for property tax purposes only on a basis consistent with its restrictions and uses.

provisions.what: To promote the conservation, preservation and continued existence of open space lands, the Legislature may define open space land

The Legislature shall provide that when this land is enforceably restricted, in a manner specified by the Legislature, to recreation, enjoyment of scenic beauty, use or conservation of natural resources, or production of food or fiber, it shall be valued for property tax purposes only on a basis that is consistent with its restrictions and uses
requires: it shall be valued for property tax purposes only on a basis that is consistent with its restrictions and uses
conditions: when this land is enforceably restricted, in a manner specified by the Legislature, to recreation, enjoyment of scenic beauty, use or conservation of natural resources, or production of food or fiber

provisions.what: To promote the preservation of property of historical significance, the Legislature may define such property

The Legislature shall provide that when it is enforceably restricted, in a manner specified by the Legislature, it shall be valued for property tax purposes only on a basis that is consistent with its restrictions and uses
requires: it shall be valued for property tax purposes only on a basis that is consistent with its restrictions and uses
conditions: when it is enforceably restricted, in a manner specified by the Legislature

review.title: Property tax postponement for seniors and disabled
review.plain: The Legislature may provide for low or moderate income persons 62 or older, and disabled persons, to postpone property taxes on their principal residence, and must provide subventions to local governments for the revenue lost.
powers: may provide by law for the manner in which a person of low or moderate income
may also provide by law for the manner in which a disabled person
shall have plenary power to define all terms in this section

provisions.what: The Legislature may provide by law for the manner in which a person of low or moderate income who is 62 years of age or older may postpone ad valorem property taxes on the dwelling owned and occupied by him or her as his or her principal place of residence

The Legislature may also provide by law for the manner in which a disabled person may postpone payment of ad valorem property taxes on the dwelling owned and occupied by him or her as his or her principal place of residence
The Legislature shall have plenary power to define all terms in this section

The Legislature shall provide by law for subventions to counties, cities and counties, cities and districts in an amount equal to the amount of revenue lost by each by reason of the postponement of taxes and for the reimbursement to the State of subventions from the payment of postponed taxes
Provision shall be made for the inclusion of reimbursement for the payment of interest on, and any costs to the State incurred in connection with, the subventions

review.title: Assessing single-family homes by use
review.plain: The Legislature may provide for assessing an owner-occupied single-family dwelling, and the land needed for its use, only on the basis of use, when it is on land zoned exclusively for single-family dwellings or agriculture.
powers: may provide for the assessment for taxation only on the basis of use of a single-family dwelling

provisions.what: The Legislature may provide for the assessment for taxation only on the basis of use of a single-family dwelling, as defined by the Legislature, and so much of the land as is required for its convenient use and occupation
conditions: when the dwelling is occupied by an owner and located on land zoned exclusively for single-family dwellings or for agricultural purposes

review.title: Assessment of nonprofit golf courses
review.plain: Real property of 10 or more acres used only for nonprofit golf course purposes for at least 2 years before the lien date is assessed on the basis of that use, plus any value from minerals or hydrocarbons.

provisions.what: Real property in a parcel of 10 or more acres which, on the lien date and for 2 or more years immediately preceding, has been used exclusively for nonprofit golf course purposes shall be assessed for taxation on the basis of such use, plus any value attributable to mines, quarries, hydrocarbon substances, or other minerals in the property or the right to extract hydrocarbons or other minerals from the property
requires: shall be assessed for taxation on the basis of such use, plus any value attributable to mines, quarries, hydrocarbon substances, or other minerals in the property or the right to extract hydrocarbons or other minerals from the property
conditions: in a parcel of 10 or more acres
on the lien date and for 2 or more years immediately preceding, has been used exclusively for nonprofit golf course purposes

review.title: Taxing local government land outside its boundaries
review.plain: Land, water rights and improvements a local government owns outside its boundaries are taxable in stated cases, chiefly in Inyo and Mono Counties, under set assessment formulas. Water-based levies between local governments are barred, and the State Board of Equalization may review these assessments.
powers: shall be subject to review, equalization, and adjustment by the State Board of Equalization
limits: shall not diminish the quantity of water rights assessable and taxable
the assessed value shall not exceed the product of
No tax, charge, assessment, or levy of any character
shall not exceed the value of all interests in the land

provisions.what: Lands owned by a local government that are outside its boundaries, including rights to use or divert water from surface or underground sources and any other interests in lands, are taxable
conditions: they are located in Inyo or Mono County and they were assessed for taxation to the local government in Inyo County as of the 1966 lien date, or in Mono County as of the 1967 lien date, whether or not the assessment was valid when made
they were acquired by the local government subsequent to that lien date and were assessed to a prior owner as of that lien date and each lien date thereafter
they are located outside Inyo or Mono County and were taxable when acquired by the local government

provisions.what: Improvements owned by a local government that are outside its boundaries are taxable
conditions: if they were taxable when acquired or were constructed by the local government to replace improvements which were taxable when acquired

provisions.what: Taxable land belonging to a local government and located in Inyo County shall be assessed in any year subsequent to 1968 at the place where it was assessed as of the 1966 lien date and in an amount derived by multiplying its 1966 assessed value by the ratio of the statewide per capita assessed value of land as of the last lien date prior to the current lien date to $766, using civilian population only

Taxable land belonging to a local government and located in Mono County shall be assessed in any year subsequent to 1968 at the place where it was assessed as of the 1967 lien date and in an amount determined by the preceding formula except that the 1967 lien date, the 1967 assessed value, and the figure $856 shall be used in the formula

Taxable land belonging to a local government and located outside of Inyo and Mono counties shall be assessed at the place where located and in an amount that does not exceed the lower of its fair market value times the prevailing percentage of fair market value at which other lands are assessed and a figure derived in the manner specified in this Section for land located in Mono County
The assessed value of the part in the base year shall be that fraction of the assessed value of the larger parcel that the area of the part is of the area of the larger parcel
conditions: If land acquired by a local government after the lien date of the base year specified in this Section was assessed in the base year as part of a larger parcel

provisions.what: The divestment shall not diminish the quantity of water rights assessable and taxable at the place where assessed as of that lien date
forbids: Diminishing the quantity of water rights assessable and taxable at the place where assessed as of that lien date
conditions: If a local government divests itself of ownership of land without water rights and this land was assessed in Inyo County as of the 1966 lien date or in Mono County as of the 1967 lien date

provisions.what: There shall be used in the computations required by Section 11(b) of this Article, for the first year for which the new percentage is applicable, in lieu of the statewide per capita assessed value of land as of the last lien date prior to the current lien date, the statewide per capita assessed value of land on the prior lien date times the ratio of the new prevailing percentage of fair market value to the previous prevailing percentage
conditions: In the event the Legislature changes the prevailing percentage of fair market value at which land is assessed for taxation

provisions.what: The replacement improvement shall be assessed, as long as it is owned by a local government, as other improvements are except that the assessed value shall not exceed the product of the percentage at which privately owned improvements are assessed times the highest full value ever used for taxation of the improvement that has been replaced
requires: For purposes of this calculation, the full value for any year prior to 1967 shall be conclusively presumed to be 4 times the assessed value in that year
forbids: An assessed value exceeding the product of the percentage at which privately owned improvements are assessed times the highest full value ever used for taxation of the improvement that has been replaced
conditions: If, after March 1954, a taxable improvement is replaced while owned by and in possession of a local government

provisions.what: No tax, charge, assessment, or levy of any character shall be imposed upon one local government by another local government that is based or calculated upon the consumption or use of water outside the boundaries of the government imposing it
forbids: Imposing upon one local government any tax, charge, assessment, or levy based or calculated upon the consumption or use of water outside the boundaries of the government imposing it
exceptions: other than those taxes authorized by Sections 11(a) to 11(d), inclusive, of this Article

provisions.what: Any taxable interest of any character in any land owned by a local government that is subject to taxation pursuant to Section 11(a) of this Article shall be taxed in the same manner as other taxable interests
exceptions: other than a lease for agricultural purposes and an interest of a local government

provisions.what: The aggregate value of all the interests subject to taxation pursuant to Section 11(a) shall not exceed the value of all interests in the land less the taxable value of the interest of any local government ascertained as provided in Sections 11(a) to 11(e), inclusive, of this Article
forbids: An aggregate value exceeding the value of all interests in the land less the taxable value of the interest of any local government

provisions.what: Any assessment made pursuant to Sections 11(a) to 11(d), inclusive, of this Article shall be subject to review, equalization, and adjustment by the State Board of Equalization
requires: an adjustment shall conform to the provisions of these Sections

review.title: Tax rates on unsecured property
review.plain: Taxes on personal property, possessory interests, and improvements on exempt land that are not secured by a lien on land are levied at the prior year's secured rates; the Legislature must adjust that rate when the assessment ratio changes.

provisions.what: Taxes on personal property, possessory interests in land, and taxable improvements located on land exempt from taxation which are not a lien upon land sufficient in value to secure their payment shall be levied at the rates for the preceding tax year upon property of the same kind where the taxes were a lien upon land sufficient in value to secure their payment
The Legislature shall adjust the rate described in subdivision (a) to maintain equality between property on the secured and unsecured rolls
conditions: In any year in which the assessment ratio is changed

review.title: Separate assessment of land and improvements
review.plain: Land and improvements must be assessed separately.

provisions.what: Land and improvements shall be separately assessed

review.title: Where local property is assessed
review.plain: All property taxed by local government must be assessed in the county, city, and district where it is located.

provisions.what: All property taxed by local government shall be assessed in the county, city, and district in which it is situated

review.title: Reassessing damaged or destroyed property
review.plain: The Legislature may authorize local government to provide for assessing or reassessing taxable property physically damaged or destroyed after the lien date.
powers: may authorize local government to provide for the assessment or reassessment of taxable property

provisions.what: The Legislature may authorize local government to provide for the assessment or reassessment of taxable property physically damaged or destroyed after the lien date to which the assessment or reassessment relates

review.title: County boards of equalization
review.plain: The county board of supervisors, or assessment appeals boards it creates, is the county board of equalization, which equalizes values on the local assessment roll. Supervisors support those boards, and the Legislature provides for their members and joint creation.
powers: may jointly create one or more assessment appeals boards

provisions.what: The county board of supervisors, or one or more assessment appeals boards created by the county board of supervisors, shall constitute the county board of equalization for a county
Two or more county boards of supervisors may jointly create one or more assessment appeals boards which shall constitute the county board of equalization for each of the participating counties
provisions.holder: Two or more county boards of supervisors

provisions.what: The county board of equalization, under such rules of notice as the county board may prescribe, shall equalize the values of all property on the local assessment roll by adjusting individual assessments
exceptions: Except as provided in subdivision (g) of Section 11

provisions.what: County boards of supervisors shall fix the compensation for members of assessment appeals boards, furnish clerical and other assistance for those boards, adopt rules of notice and procedures for those boards as may be required to facilitate their work and to insure uniformity in the processing and decision of equalization petitions
County boards of supervisors may provide for their discontinuance

The Legislature shall provide for the number and qualifications of members of assessment appeals boards, the manner of selecting, appointing, and removing them, and the terms for which they serve, and the procedure by which two or more county boards of supervisors may jointly create one or more assessment appeals boards

review.title: State Board of Equalization membership
review.plain: The Board of Equalization has 5 voting members: the Controller and 4 members elected from four districts for 4-year terms at gubernatorial elections. No member may serve more than 2 terms.
limits: No member may serve more than 2 terms

provisions.what: The Board of Equalization consists of 5 voting members: the Controller and 4 members elected for 4-year terms at gubernatorial elections
The State shall be divided into four Board of Equalization districts with the voters of each district electing one member
No member may serve more than 2 terms

review.title: Equalizing county assessment levels
review.plain: The Board must measure county assessment levels each year and bring them into conformity by adjusting entire secured local rolls. If the State levies a property tax, remaining unequal levels are corrected for distributing that tax.

provisions.what: The Board shall measure county assessment levels annually and shall bring those levels into conformity by adjusting entire secured local assessment rolls

The effects of unequalized local assessment levels, to the extent any remain after such adjustments, shall be corrected for purposes of distributing this tax by equalizing the assessment levels of locally and state-assessed properties and varying the rate of the state tax inversely with the counties’ respective assessment levels
conditions: In the event a property tax is levied by the State

review.title: State assessment of utility property
review.plain: The Board must assess each year multi-county pipelines, canals and aqueducts and the property of regulated railway, telegraph, telephone, gas and electric companies. Those companies may not face differing taxes or license charges; the Board may delegate some assessment to local assessors.
powers: may authorize Board assessment of property owned or used by other public utilities
may delegate to a local assessor the duty to assess a property
limits: No other tax or license charge may be imposed on these companies

provisions.what: The Board shall annually assess pipelines, flumes, canals, ditches, and aqueducts lying within 2 or more counties and property, except franchises, owned or used by regulated railway, telegraph, or telephone companies, car companies operating on railways in the State, and companies transmitting or selling gas or electricity
requires: This property shall be subject to taxation to the same extent and in the same manner as other property

provisions.what: No other tax or license charge may be imposed on these companies which differs from that imposed on mercantile, manufacturing, and other business corporations
forbids: Imposing on these companies any other tax or license charge which differs from that imposed on mercantile, manufacturing, and other business corporations
exceptions: This restriction does not release a utility company from payments agreed on or required by law for a special privilege or franchise granted by a government body

provisions.what: The Legislature may authorize Board assessment of property owned or used by other public utilities
The Board may delegate to a local assessor the duty to assess a property used but not owned by a state assessee on which the taxes are to be paid by a local assessee

review.title: Local tax rate and bonding limits
review.plain: The Legislature may provide maximum property tax rates and bonding limits for local governments.
powers: may provide maximum property tax rates and bonding limits for local governments

provisions.what: The Legislature may provide maximum property tax rates and bonding limits for local governments

review.title: School district tax levies
review.plain: Within any limits under Section 20, the Legislature must provide for county governing bodies to levy each year school district taxes sufficient to produce the revenues each district’s board determines its schools and functions require.

provisions.what: The Legislature shall provide for an annual levy by county governing bodies of school district taxes sufficient to produce annual revenues for each district that the district’s board determines are required for its schools and district functions
conditions: Within such limits as may be provided under Section 20 of this Article

review.title: Cap on state property tax revenue
review.plain: Not more than 25 percent of the State's total appropriations from all funds may be raised by taxes on real and personal property according to its value.
limits: Not more than 25 percent of the total appropriations from all funds of the State

provisions.what: Not more than 25 percent of the total appropriations from all funds of the State shall be raised by means of taxes on real and personal property according to the value thereof
forbids: Raising more than 25 percent of the total appropriations from all funds of the State by means of taxes on real and personal property according to the value thereof

review.title: Taxing property after boundary changes
review.plain: If the state's boundaries change, the Legislature must determine how the affected property is taxed.

provisions.what: The Legislature shall determine how property affected shall be taxed

review.title: Local taxes and local tax proceeds
review.plain: The Legislature may not impose taxes for local purposes but may authorize local governments to impose them, and may not take or redirect proceeds of local taxes levied solely for local purposes. State money given to local governments may be used as provided.
powers: may authorize local governments to impose them
limits: may not impose taxes for local purposes
may not reallocate, transfer, borrow, appropriate, restrict the use of, or otherwise use the proceeds

provisions.what: The Legislature may not impose taxes for local purposes
The Legislature may authorize local governments to impose taxes for local purposes

The Legislature may not reallocate, transfer, borrow, appropriate, restrict the use of, or otherwise use the proceeds of any tax imposed or levied by a local government solely for the local government’s purposes
forbids: Reallocating, transferring, borrowing, appropriating, restricting the use of, or otherwise using the proceeds of any tax imposed or levied by a local government solely for the local government’s purposes

provisions.what: Money appropriated from state funds to a local government for its local purposes may be used as provided by law
Money subvened to a local government under Section 25 may be used for state or local purposes
